instruction: Add "none.png" from the Desktop to slide 2 with a size of 2cm × 2cm.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated to slide 2, inserted none.png via Insert > Image menu, then resized the image to 1cm x 1cm using the Position and Size panel.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select slides in panel, use Insert > Image menu to add images, navigate file dialog, resize images using Position and Size properties.
metadata.task_rationale: Same slide target but with a larger square size (2cm x 2cm instead of 1cm x 1cm), testing the model handles different dimension values correctly.
metadata.explanation: Custom getter reads slide 2 (index 1) image properties from the pptx. Metric checks if at least one image exists with 2cm width and 2cm height (0.05cm tolerance). Partial credit: 0.5 for image presence, 0.5 for correct size.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads slide 2 (index 1) and extracts all PICTURE shapes with dimensions in cm (EMU/360000 conversion is correct).
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses expected.get('expected_width_cm') without unwrapping a 'rules' key.
Partial credit scoring is sensible: 0.5 for image presence, 0.5 for correct 2cm x 2cm dimensions with 0.05cm tolerance.
Postconfig properly activates the window and saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads the pptx, ensuring fresh state.

Minor gap: Evaluator does not verify that the added image is specifically 'none.png' — it only checks that ANY image with matching dimensions exists on slide 2. If the slide had a pre-existing image of the same size, this could yield a false positive.

The instruction requirement to add the image FROM the Desktop is not verified (only presence and size are checked), but this is acceptable since the end-state check is the standard verification approach.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider checking the image name or blob content to verify the specific image 'none.png' was added, rather than accepting any image with matching dimensions.
